questions.question_text: Which of the following best captures the meaning of a supply chain?

options.A: The network of factories that manufacture a product
options.B: The transportation system used to move finished goods
options.C: All parties involved, directly or indirectly, in fulfilling a customer request
options.D: The warehousing and inventory activities of a firm

questions.explanation: A supply chain is an end-to-end system that encompasses all entities, processes, and flows directly or indirectly involved in fulfilling a customer request.

questions.question_text: Which set of flows moves continuously within a supply chain?

options.A: Product, advertising, and labour
options.B: Product, information, and funds
options.C: Inventory, machinery, and discounts
options.D: Production, retailing, and branding

questions.explanation: Every supply chain relies on three primary interconnected flows: physical product/material flow, bi-directional information flow, and financial cash/funds flow.

questions.question_text: What is the primary objective of a supply chain?

options.A: To maximize the manufacturer’s profit
options.B: To minimize transportation cost alone
options.C: To maximize overall value generated, or supply chain surplus
options.D: To keep inventory as low as possible

questions.explanation: The primary objective of a supply chain is to maximize the total Supply Chain Surplus created across all stages, rather than locally optimizing an individual firm's profits.

questions.question_text: Supply chain surplus is best expressed as:

options.A: Revenue minus manufacturing cost
options.B: Profit margin multiplied by asset turnover
options.C: Price paid by customer minus retailer margin
options.D: Customer value minus supply chain cost

questions.explanation: Supply Chain Surplus is defined as the total Customer Value (maximum willingness to pay) minus the total costs incurred across all stages of the supply chain.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is most clearly a supply chain design decision rather than a planning or operations decision?

options.A: Choosing the location of warehouses for the next several years
options.B: Assigning today’s customer orders to specific trucks
options.C: Deciding monthly inventory targets for the festive season
options.D: Creating pick lists for a warehouse shift

questions.explanation: Supply chain design decisions involve long-term architectural choices (spanning years), such as facility location and capacity choices, which cannot be easily altered in the short term.

questions.question_text: In the cycle view of supply chain processes, the replenishment cycle occurs at the interface between:

options.A: Customer and retailer
options.B: Retailer and distributor or warehouse
options.C: Manufacturer and supplier
options.D: Distributor and customer

questions.explanation: In the cycle view, the replenishment cycle takes place at the interface between the retailer and the distributor/warehouse as the retailer replenishes inventory to satisfy customer demand.

questions.question_text: In the push or pull view, a process is classified as a pull process if it is:

options.A: Executed in anticipation of customer orders
options.B: Executed only by the manufacturer
options.C: Initiated in response to a customer order
options.D: Always performed with low inventory

questions.explanation: Pull processes are triggered directly in response to an explicit customer order, whereas push processes operate speculatively in anticipation of demand.

questions.question_text: What does strategic fit mean?

options.A: Choosing the lowest-cost supplier in every category
options.B: Matching the responsiveness of the supply chain to the uncertainty created by the competitive strategy
options.C: Maximizing inventory turns regardless of service level
options.D: Ensuring that every stage of the supply chain is equally responsive

questions.explanation: Strategic fit requires aligning the operational capabilities of the supply chain (responsiveness vs. efficiency) with the implied demand uncertainty generated by the firm's competitive strategy.

questions.question_text: Return on equity, ROE, is defined as:

options.A: Net income divided by average total assets
options.B: Earnings before interest divided by sales revenue
options.C: Sales revenue divided by average shareholder equity
options.D: Net income divided by average shareholder equity

questions.explanation: Return on Equity (ROE) measures financial profitability relative to shareholder investment and is calculated as Net Income divided by Average Shareholder Equity.

questions.question_text: According to Little’s Law, if throughput is 60 units per day and average flow time is 4 days, average inventory in the system is:

options.A: 15 units
options.B: 56 units
options.C: 64 units
options.D: 240 units

questions.explanation: According to Little's Law ($I = D \times T$), Average Inventory ($I$) = Throughput ($D$) $\times$ Flow Time ($T$). Substituting the given values: $I = 60 \text{ units/day} \times 4 \text{ days} = 240 \text{ units}$.

questions.question_text: Why is forecasting important even in a pull-based supply chain?

options.A: Because pull systems do not need actual customer orders
options.B: Because capacity and inventory still need to be planned in advance
options.C: Because forecasting replaces collaboration
options.D: Because pull systems eliminate uncertainty

questions.explanation: Although pull execution responds to actual customer orders, long-lead resources, operational capacity, and baseline inventory buffers must still be planned ahead using demand forecasts.

questions.question_text: What is the main benefit of collaborative forecasting?

options.A: It ensures every stage uses a different forecast
options.B: It eliminates the need for buffer inventory
options.C: It helps supply chain partners align around a common view of demand
options.D: It works only for long-range forecasts

questions.explanation: Collaborative forecasting shares market insights and promotional plans across supply chain partners to establish a single aligned view of future demand, mitigating supply-demand mismatches.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a common feature of most forecasts?

options.A: They are equally accurate for individual SKUs and broad categories
options.B: They are usually more accurate for groups than for individual items
options.C: Their accuracy improves as the time horizon increases
options.D: They are always perfect if data is available

questions.explanation: Forecasts are significantly more accurate for aggregated groups or product families because individual SKU variations and random demand fluctuations cancel each other out.

questions.question_text: If a forecast is too low, which of the following is most likely?

options.A: Excess inventory and idle capacity
options.B: Lower holding costs and better service
options.C: Better coordination with suppliers
options.D: Stockouts, missed deliveries, and poor service

questions.explanation: Under-forecasting leads to insufficient inventory positioning and capacity allocation, resulting in stock-outs, fulfillment delays, and eroded customer service levels.

questions.question_text: A time series that fluctuates around a fairly stable average level, with no clear upward or downward movement, is best described as:

options.A: Trend
options.B: Seasonal
options.C: Horizontal
options.D: Cyclical

questions.explanation: A horizontal (or level) pattern represents time-series data that fluctuates randomly around a constant mean value without any sustained upward or downward trend.

questions.question_text: What is the key difference between seasonality and cyclical variation?

options.A: Seasonality is random, while cycles are fixed
options.B: Seasonality repeats with a known periodicity, while cycles do not have a fixed periodicity
options.C: Cycles occur weekly, while seasonality occurs yearly
options.D: Cycles are easier to forecast than seasonality

questions.explanation: Seasonality consists of regular demand movements tied to recurring calendar events with a known, fixed periodicity. Cyclical variations are long-term macroeconomic shifts with non-fixed periods.

questions.question_text: If actual demand is 100 and forecast demand is 90, then the forecast error is:
questions.explanation: Forecast error is defined as $E_t = A_t - F_t$. Substituting the values: $E_t = 100 - 90 = +10$.

questions.question_text: Which forecast accuracy measure penalizes large errors more heavily because the errors are squared?

options.A: MAD
options.B: MSE
options.C: MAPE
options.D: Mean forecast

questions.explanation: Mean Squared Error (MSE) squares individual errors $(A_t - F_t)^2$, which heavily penalizes large forecast deviations relative to smaller errors.

questions.question_text: Suppose the previous forecast is 42, actual demand is 40, and α = 0.10. What is the new exponential smoothing forecast?
questions.explanation: Using the Single Exponential Smoothing formula: $F_t = F_{t-1} + \alpha (A_{t-1} - F_{t-1}) = 42 + 0.10(40 - 42) = 42 + 0.10(-2) = 42 - 0.2 = 41.8$.

questions.question_text: Which statement best captures the purpose of aggregate planning?

options.A: To determine the exact SKU picked for each customer order tomorrow
options.B: To decide detailed truck routes for the coming week
options.C: To plan production, capacity, inventory, and backlogs over the next few months profitably
options.D: To estimate the intercept and slope of a trend line

questions.explanation: Aggregate planning determines aggregate output rates, workforce levels, inventory levels, and backlogs over an intermediate planning horizon (3 to 18 months) to satisfy demand at minimum total cost.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best defines inventory?

options.A: Only finished goods waiting to be sold
options.B: A stock or store of goods
options.C: Only raw materials used in manufacturing
options.D: Goods that are obsolete and unsold

questions.explanation: Inventory is defined broadly as any stock or store of physical goods (including raw materials, WIP, finished goods, and MRO) held within a supply chain.

questions.question_text: Safety stock is best described as:

options.A: Inventory created only because of quantity discounts
options.B: Inventory used only in manufacturing
options.C: Inventory that is obsolete and marked down
options.D: Inventory held in excess of expected demand to compensate for demand and lead-time variability

questions.explanation: Safety stock is buffer inventory maintained above baseline expected demand to protect the firm against demand surges and vendor lead-time delays.

questions.question_text: According to Little’s Law, if average demand is 5 units per day and average time in the system is 10 days, average inventory is:

options.A: 15 units
options.B: 50 units
options.C: 100 units
options.D: 2 units

questions.explanation: According to Little's Law ($I = D \times T$), Average Inventory ($I$) = Demand Rate ($D$) $\times$ Flow Time ($T$). Thus, $I = 5 \text{ units/day} \times 10 \text{ days} = 50 \text{ units}$.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not one of the four basic inventory cost categories discussed in class?

options.A: Purchase cost
options.B: Holding cost
options.C: Shortage cost
options.D: Advertising cost

questions.explanation: The four main inventory cost categories are Purchase Cost, Holding Cost, Ordering/Setup Cost, and Shortage Cost. Advertising is a marketing expense.

questions.question_text: If an item costs ₹180 per unit and the annual carrying-rate is 10%, what is the annual holding cost per unit
questions.explanation: Annual holding cost per unit ($h$) is calculated as $h = i \times C$. Substituting the given values: $h = 10\% \times ₹180 = ₹18$ per unit per year.

questions.question_text: Which statement best describes ordering cost?

options.A: It is always proportional only to the number of units ordered
options.B: It is the same as shortage cost
options.C: It includes only purchase spending
options.D: It usually has a fixed component per order

questions.explanation: Ordering cost represents administrative, clerical, and transportation costs that contain a fixed component ($K$) incurred each time an order run is placed, independent of the order lot size $Q$.

questions.question_text: In ABC classification, “A” items are typically:

options.A: A large fraction of items with a small share of annual value
options.B: A small fraction of items with a large share of annual value
options.C: The cheapest items in the system
options.D: Items with zero stockout risk

questions.explanation: Based on the Pareto Principle (80/20 rule), Class A items represent a small fraction of total inventory SKUs (10–20%) but account for the vast majority of annual dollar usage value (60–70%).

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a key assumption of the basic EOQ model?

options.A: Demand is uncertain and follows a normal distribution
options.B: Shortages are allowed and backordered
options.C: Demand is deterministic and occurs at a constant rate
options.D: Quantity discounts always exist

questions.explanation: The basic Ford Harris Economic Order Quantity (EOQ) model assumes that demand is known with certainty (deterministic) and is consumed at a constant rate over time.

questions.question_text: In the basic EOQ model, average inventory over a cycle is:

options.A: D/Q
options.B: Q

questions.explanation: In the basic EOQ model, inventory follows a constant sawtooth pattern starting at lot size $Q$ down to $0$, resulting in an average cycle inventory of $Q/2$.

questions.question_text: According to EOQ logic, if ordering cost K increases while all else stays constant, the optimal order quantity will:

options.A: Increase
options.B: Decrease
options.C: Stay unchanged
options.D: Become zero

questions.explanation: The EOQ formula is $Q^* = \sqrt{\frac{2DK}{h}}$. Because $Q^*$ is directly proportional to $\sqrt{K}$, an increase in fixed ordering cost $K$ increases the optimal order size $Q^*$ to amortize the higher order cost over more units.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes sourcing in the course?

options.A: Only vendor selection
options.B: Only procurement execution
options.C: The broader system of acquiring materials, services, and capabilities, including selection, contracting, coordination, and performance management
options.D: Only contract negotiation

questions.explanation: Sourcing is an end-to-end organizational system that combines supplier evaluation, contracting, design collaboration, procurement execution, and supplier performance analytics.

questions.question_text: What is the key difference between outsourcing and offshoring?

options.A: Outsourcing is about location; offshoring is about ownership
options.B: Outsourcing is about who performs the activity; offshoring is about where the activity is performed
options.C: They mean exactly the same thing
options.D: Outsourcing is domestic only; offshoring is international only

questions.explanation: Outsourcing determines entity ownership (shifting internal work to a third party), whereas offshoring determines geography (moving execution to a foreign country).

questions.question_text: An outsourcing decision should primarily be judged by:

options.A: Unit purchase price alone
options.B: Whether the third party increases total supply chain surplus after accounting for risk
options.C: Whether the supplier is larger than the firm
options.D: Whether the supplier is offshore

questions.explanation: An outsourcing decision is economically viable if the third party generates higher total Supply Chain Surplus ($	ext{Customer Value} - 	ext{Total System Cost}$) net of coordination friction and risks.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best distinguishes a 3PL from a 4PL?

options.A: A 3PL always owns the inventory, while a 4PL never does
options.B: A 3PL works only in transportation, while a 4PL works only in warehousing
options.C: A 3PL is domestic, while a 4PL is global
options.D: A 3PL typically executes logistics activities, while a 4PL primarily orchestrates a broader end-to-end logistics network

questions.explanation: A 3PL provides physical logistics services (transport, warehousing), whereas a 4PL acts as an overarching neutral integrator managing multiple 3PL providers, IT systems, and processes.

questions.question_text: Why is supplier evaluation based only on quoted price considered a mistake?

options.A: Because price is usually unobservable
options.B: Because quoted prices are always manipulated
options.C: Because the relevant criterion is total cost, which includes inventory, delivery, quality, and support costs as well
options.D: Because lower price always implies worse quality

questions.explanation: Focusing solely on unit price ignores total cost factors (Total Cost of Ownership - TCO), such as inventory carrying costs driven by lead times, freight fees, defect quality costs, and administrative overhead.

questions.question_text: Which contract type is most directly intended to reduce the retailer’s downside risk from leftover inventory?

options.A: Buyback contract
options.B: Quantity discount contract
options.C: Two-part tariff
options.D: Shared-savings contract

questions.explanation: In a buyback contract, the manufacturer agrees to buy back unsold stock at a agreed salvage price, shifting overstock risk away from the retailer to encourage higher order levels.

questions.question_text: In a revenue-sharing contract, the supplier typically:

options.A: Charges a higher wholesale price and keeps all retail revenue
options.B: Charges a lower wholesale price and receives a fraction of sales revenue
options.C: Eliminates all forecasting risk for the retailer
options.D: Guarantees a fixed service level without compensation

questions.explanation: Under revenue-sharing contracts, the manufacturer lowers the initial unit wholesale price $w$, in exchange for receiving a percentage fraction $f$ of the retailer's downstream sales revenues.

questions.question_text: Which contract is mainly aimed at motivating a supplier to improve process performance, such as lead time reduction or quality improvement?

options.A: Buyback contract
options.B: Quantity discount contract
options.C: Shared-savings contract
options.D: Simple wholesale-price-only contract

questions.explanation: A shared-savings contract incentivizes suppliers to invest capital in performance improvements (e.g., lead-time compression, defect reduction) by sharing the resulting supply chain financial savings.

questions.question_text: Why is design collaboration important from a supply chain perspective?

options.A: Because it matters only to engineering aesthetics
options.B: Because it allows suppliers to influence manufacturability, commonality, and logistics costs early in the design stage
options.C: Because it guarantees low prices later
options.D: Because it removes the need for contracts

questions.explanation: Early supplier involvement in product design directly impacts 60–80% of end-to-end supply chain costs by driving component standardization, manufacturability, and transport packaging efficiency.

questions.question_text: Tailored sourcing means:

options.A: Combining different types of suppliers because different products need different strengths
options.B: Using one supplier for every product to simplify management
options.C: Always preferring offshore suppliers for mature products
options.D: Always preferring responsive suppliers for every SKU

questions.explanation: Tailored sourcing allocates demand across a portfolio of sources—for instance, contracting efficient, low-cost suppliers for baseline predictable demand, while using flexible, responsive suppliers for uncertain demand surges.

questions.question_text: The evolution of the Milk supply chain had many concepts. Which of the following was NOT a key concept?

options.A: Delayed Differentiation (Postponement)
options.B: Cash Logistics
options.C: Quality assessment
options.D: Packaging

questions.explanation: The Indian milk supply chain (Amul) leveraged rapid cash logistics, village-level quality/fat testing, and processing/packaging, but did not rely on delayed differentiation (postponement), which applies to industries like paint and apparel.

questions.question_text: The primary driver for a new Supply Chain Strategy in FarmAid Tractors was

options.A: Sales were going down
options.B: End of month spike in sales
options.C: Seasonality
options.D: Delivered quality to the dealer

questions.explanation: In the FarmAid Tractors case, approximately 70% of tractors delivered to dealers were not ready for immediate sale due to transit damage, missing components, or unrectified factory defects, driving the supply chain re-engineering strategy.

questions.question_text: The locations of stockyards in FarmAid Tractors were being reconsidered because:

options.A: Current locations were driven by the Marketing office rather than Logistics.
options.B: Secondary movement was to shift from own driving to truck-based delivery.
options.C: Both the reasons
options.D: None of the reasons

questions.explanation: Legacy stockyards were sub-optimally tied to regional marketing offices (causing freight backtracking) and the secondary delivery model was transitioning from self-driving on roads to damage-free truck transports.

questions.question_text: In the Tea supply chain, Auctions play an important role. Which of the following is NOT a benefit of Auctions?

options.A: Quality assessment
options.B: Blending choices
options.C: Logistics costs
options.D: Price discovery

questions.explanation: Centralized tea auctions provide transparent price discovery, quality assessment by tasters, and blending flexibility, but they introduce extra handling layers, delays, and higher total logistics costs.

questions.question_text: The Milk supply chain has evolved leveraging

options.A: Both Forward and Backward integration
options.B: Forward integration only
options.C: Backward integration only
options.D: Neither Forward nor Backward integration, but due to other factors

questions.explanation: The cooperative milk model (Amul) forward integrated into processing, cold-chain distribution, and retail outlets, while backward integrating into cattle feed plants, veterinary support, and breeding centers.

questions.question_text: In the reengineered Paint supply chain, benefits accrued due to

options.A: Increased ability to accept returns
options.B: Better match between demand and supply
options.C: Higher inventories
options.D: Quicker delivery to the customer

questions.explanation: By shifting from manufacturing hundreds of pre-colored paint SKUs to distributing base paints and mixing custom tint pigments at retail stores (postponement), supply was perfectly matched with real-time customer demand.

questions.question_text: Horizontal unbundling of supply chains focussing on market segments addresses the need for:

options.A: Cost efficiencies
options.B: Specialization and customisation
options.C: Scale economies
options.D: Scope economies

questions.explanation: Horizontal unbundling structures distinct, dedicated supply chain channels for specific market segments to deliver operational specialization and tailored customization.

questions.question_text: Product redesign should concern itself with

options.A: Only buyer interest
options.B: Only logistics
options.C: Both buyer interest and logistics

questions.explanation: Product redesign for supply chain efficiency must simultaneously satisfy customer/buyer value preferences while optimizing physical transport density, package cube utilization, and handling logistics.

questions.question_text: What was the primary role of distributors in JOSH Denims' original supply chain structure?

options.A: To deliver directly from the C and FA warehouse to consumers
options.B: To absorb operational and financial risks by holding inventory and managing retailer demand fluctuations
options.C: To manufacture denim garments for JOSH Denims
options.D: To manage international shipping and customs clearance

questions.explanation: Distributors in the original network held local buffer stock, extended credit to retailers, and managed local demand fluctuations. This absorbed operational and financial risks before goods reached the retail tier.

questions.question_text: Why did JOSH Denims remove the distributor tier?

options.A: To gain more control and capture distributor margins
options.B: To comply with new government rules
options.C: To transfer manufacturing to the C and FA
options.D: To outsource all logistics to an international provider

questions.explanation: Removing distributors allowed JOSH Denims to practice disintermediation, capturing distributor margins and establishing direct contact and control over retail channels.

questions.question_text: What role does cold storage play in agricultural supply chains?

options.A: It removes the need for wholesale markets
options.B: It acts as an inventory buffer for seasonal produce
options.C: It replaces traders and commission agents
options.D: It helps sort agricultural produce

questions.explanation: Cold storage acts as a seasonal inventory buffer connecting perishable harvest periods with year-round demand. It helps stabilize supply and prevents distress selling by farmers during harvest gluts.

questions.question_text: What was the key strategic decision facing Hasmukhbhai?

options.A: Whether to exit cold storage
options.B: Which city - Surat, Pune or Mumbai - offered the best expansion opportunity
options.C: Whether to serve only farmers
options.D: Whether to move into retailing

questions.explanation: Hasmukhbhai evaluated expansion opportunities for a 5,000-tonne cold storage facility across candidate cities (Surat, Pune, and Mumbai), analyzing trade-offs in capital costs and local market demand.

questions.question_text: Why did Rajashree Cement explore the Engine on Load scheme?

options.A: To comply with a rule requiring rail transport.
options.B: To expand direct retail delivery.
options.C: To replace grinding units.
options.D: To increase throughput of bulk cement.

questions.explanation: The Engine on Load (EOL) scheme keeps the locomotive attached during loading/unloading, drastically reducing rake turnaround times to increase overall bulk cement dispatch throughput.

questions.question_text: What product was Rajashree Cement transporting which needed analysis?

options.A: Bulk cement
options.B: Packaged cement bags
options.C: Fly ash
options.D: Clinker

questions.explanation: The transport analysis focused on bulk cement dispatches via private rakes between the Malkhaid plant and the Doddaballapur unloading/bagging hub.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was NOT a core business service offered by Shreeji Transport Services?

options.A: Less-than-truckload cargo consolidation
options.B: Express parcel
options.C: Full Truck Load transportation services
options.D: Temperature-controlled refrigerated logistics

questions.explanation: Shreeji Transport offered Full Truck Load, Less-than-truckload, bonded trucking, and parcel express services, but did not specialize in temperature-controlled refrigerated logistics.

questions.question_text: Which managerial focus is most relevant for route profitability?

options.A: Increasing the number of trucks
options.B: Avoiding long term customer contracts
options.C: Price setting based on route analysis, including load availability at the destination
options.D: Reducing shipment documentation

questions.explanation: Route profitability depends on setting pricing based on granular route analysis, considering turnaround time, freight rate density, and backhaul load availability rather than distance alone.

questions.question_text: What does the Operating Ratio for Indian Railways primarily indicate?

options.A: The amount spent in rupees to earn every 100 rupees of revenue.
options.B: The percentage of profits reinvested into network infrastructure upgrades.
options.C: The total capital expenditure required to maintain the existing railway lines.
options.D: The ratio of passenger revenue to freight revenue across all its zones.

questions.explanation: The Operating Ratio measures operational efficiency by indicating the amount in rupees spent by Indian Railways to earn 100 rupees of gross revenue.

questions.question_text: What is the primary competitive disadvantage for Indian Railways' freight services when compared to road transport?

options.A: Significantly higher freight charges for bulk commodities such as coal, iron ore and cement.
options.B: Inability to carry oversized or heavy industrial equipment due to track and tunnel limitations.
options.C: A more complex and time-consuming booking and documentation process for consignments.
options.D: Lack of reliable first- and last-mile connectivity, making it less suitable for door-to-door service.

questions.explanation: Indian Railways lacks seamless first- and last-mile connectivity, making road transport preferred for flexible, door-to-door delivery despite higher long-haul line-haul costs.

questions.question_text: Which characteristic best describes the ownership structure of the Indian road freight transport industry?

options.A: It is dominated by a few large multinational corporations that control major national routes and contracts.
options.B: It is highly fragmented, with a large majority of operators owning very small fleets, often five trucks or fewer.
options.C: It is primarily composed of medium-sized regional companies that specialise in specific types of cargo.
options.D: It is largely state-owned, with government-run corporations handling most long-haul freight movement.

questions.explanation: The Indian trucking industry is highly fragmented, with nearly 75% of operators owning small fleets of five or fewer trucks.

questions.question_text: Which expenses typically constitutes the largest single component of total operating costs for a truck operator in India?

options.A: Driver salaries and related benefits, which have been rising steadily due to a shortage of skilled drivers.
options.B: Fuel costs, which are also volatile.
options.C: Maintenance and repair costs, including tyres and spare parts, for keeping vehicles roadworthy.
options.D: Toll charges and inter-state taxes, which add up significantly on long-haul routes.

questions.explanation: Fuel costs constitute the largest single operating expense for long-haul truck operators in India, often accounting for over 40-50% of total running costs.

questions.question_text: In a Public-Private Partnership for a port terminal, what is the primary purpose of the Concession Agreement?

options.A: It is a short-term permit that allows a shipping line to use the port facilities for a single voyage.
options.B: It is a financial statement detailing the projected revenue and profitability of the terminal for investors.
options.C: It is a legal contract defining the rights, obligations and risk allocation for the private operator and the port authority.
options.D: It is a marketing document used by the port authority to attract new shipping lines and cargo to the terminal.

questions.explanation: A Concession Agreement is a formal legal contract between the public port authority and the private concessionaire specifying performance obligations, operational rights, revenue sharing, and risk allocation.

questions.question_text: Why is efficient hinterland connectivity considered critical for the commercial success of a new private port terminal?

options.A: It allows the port to attract more cruise ships and tourism, thereby diversifying revenue streams.
options.B: It directly determines the tariff rates that the port terminal is legally allowed to charge customers.
options.C: It ensures a smooth and cost-effective flow of cargo between the port and industrial or consumption centres.
options.D: It is the primary factor considered by the government when awarding environmental clearances for port projects.

questions.explanation: Hinterland rail and road connectivity ensures fast, reliable, and cost-effective evacuation of cargo between maritime berths and inland consumption/manufacturing centers.

questions.question_text: Sea as a mode choice is preferred from many of the sources for Laxmi Transformers. This is because

options.A: Rail is a complex mode requiring supply chain coordination with a difficult bureaucracy.
options.B: It is difficult to procure the required number of trucks.
options.C: Ships are easy to charter at low prices.
options.D: The holding costs of the raw material are low, enabling large volume handling required for a ship.

questions.explanation: Iron ore and pellets have relatively low inventory holding costs per ton, making low-cost bulk ocean shipment (large shipment lot sizes) economical despite longer transit times.

questions.question_text: Laxmi Transformers has a competitive advantage in serving the integrated steel plant markets in Eastern India because

options.A: Steel plants are a reliable buyer of sponge iron.
options.B: The return empty of the ship provides a supply opportunity at marginal costs.
options.C: This market can be used as a ‘buffer’ if there is any excess after supplying the mini steel plants.
options.D: Rail connectivity is available for direct unloading at the steel plants, thereby saving last-mile costs.

questions.explanation: Time-chartered ships carrying inbound ore from Eastern ports return empty to the East. Utilizing this empty backhaul to transport outbound sponge iron drastically lowers marginal freight costs.

questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of the LEADS index?

options.A: To measure export performance across Indian states.
options.B: To evaluate logistics efficiency across Indian states.
options.C: To rank private logistics companies in India.
options.D: To compare port performance across coastal states.

questions.explanation: The LEADS (Logistics Ease Across Different States) index assesses and ranks the performance and efficiency of the logistics ecosystem across Indian states and Union Territories.

questions.question_text: Which institution’s Logistics Performance Index influenced the development of LEADS?

options.A: World Trade Organization.
options.B: International Monetary Fund.
options.C: Asian Development Bank.
options.D: World Bank.

questions.explanation: LEADS was developed by the Ministry of Commerce & Industry based on the framework of the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index (LPI).

questions.question_text: Which two indicators were added in LEADS 2018 beyond the broad Logistics Performance Index style indicators?

options.A: Favorability of operating environment and safety/security of cargo movement.
options.B: Green logistics commitment and women’s participation in logistics workforce.
options.C: Packaging facilities and grievance redressal under regulatory environment.
options.D: Warehouse approvals and ease of entry into neighbouring states.

questions.explanation: LEADS 2018 added 'Favorability of operating environment' and 'Safety/security of cargo movement' to capture domestic regulatory and operational conditions specific to Indian states.

questions.question_text: Why were states later grouped into coastal, landlocked, north-eastern and union territory categories?

options.A: To reduce the number of indicators used in the ranking.
options.B: To give coastal states a higher score by default.
options.C: To compare states more fairly based on geographic context.
options.D: To normalize the investments by state governments for logistics.

questions.explanation: Categorizing states based on geography ensures a fair comparison by accounting for structural differences in port access, terrain, and regional infrastructure challenges.

questions.question_text: What was the primary objective of the mid-day meal programme?

options.A: To improve nutrition and encourage regular school attendance.
options.B: To replace all school-based cooking with centralised kitchens.
options.C: To increase the number of government schools in rural areas.
options.D: To provide packaged food to children in government schools so they could take it home.

questions.explanation: The Midday Meal Program aims to combat classroom hunger, improve child nutrition, and incentivize regular enrollment and attendance among school children.

questions.question_text: Why did the Gujarat government approach Akshaya Patra for further expansion?

options.A: Because the Government wanted to introduce meals service to the poor.
options.B: Because the foundation had unused vehicles across all locations.
options.C: Because they wanted the meals service in Government hospital.
options.D: Because there was going to be a sharp increase in the number of rural schools.

questions.explanation: Impressed by Akshaya Patra's efficient centralized meal distribution, the government approached them to expand operations into providing dietary meal services in Government hospitals.

questions.question_text: Why was the centralised kitchen model more suitable for urban areas?

options.A: Urban schools needed fewer meals than rural schools.
options.B: Urban schools had lesser space for setting up in-school kitchens.
options.C: Urban schools were usually geographically closer to one another.
options.D: Land was easier to procure for a centralised kitchen.

questions.explanation: In urban areas, schools are clustered close together geographically, allowing centralized kitchens to achieve high transport utilization and deliver warm meals within strict time windows.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was NOT a government specified regulation to be satisfied by Akshaya Patra?
